notes.subject: תחגרנה
notes.rationale: 'di apara seaparo' — literally 'they gird themselves with joy', the image of joy as a garment/belt bound on.

notes.subject: וגיל
notes.rationale: May be noun 'joy' (girded with joy) or place-name Gil/Gilead ('the hills gird Gil'); most versions take 'joy'.

notes.subject: מדבר
notes.rationale: Open grazing land, not dead sand-desert; 'nagakgole' captures the dry wilderness pasture.

translation: Dipastara tša nagakgole di nalediša; gomme thabanyana di apara boitumelo bjalo ka seaparo.
